persona_catalog.label: Default Traveller
persona_catalog.description: No declared constraints. Balanced ranking optimising for experience quality, value, safety and ease of travel.

persona_catalog.label: Friends Trip
persona_catalog.description: Group of 3-8 adults, no children, mixed budget sensitivity, high appetite for shared activities, nightlife and photo-worthy moments. Per-head cost matters more than luxury.

persona_catalog.label: Family Trip
persona_catalog.description: Two or more adults travelling with children (3-17). Optimises for safety, kid engagement, short transfers, dining ease and medical fallback. Nightlife is actively de-prioritised.

persona_catalog.label: Bachelor Trip
persona_catalog.description: All-male (or predominantly male) pre-wedding group. Nightlife, adult entertainment, day-drinking, adventure and per-head cost dominate. Cultural/heritage weight near zero.

persona_catalog.label: Bachelorette Trip
persona_catalog.description: All-female (or predominantly female) pre-wedding group. Balances nightlife and photo-forward experiences with a materially higher safety floor, plus wellness/spa and beach-club weighting.

persona_catalog.label: First International Trip
persona_catalog.description: Traveller has never left the country. Optimises for low-friction entry, English usability, mature tourist infrastructure, low scam pressure, direct flights and food familiarity. Novelty is secondary to confidence.

persona_catalog.label: Content Creator
persona_catalog.description: Traveller monetising or building an audience. Optimises for visual payload, novelty (low saturation), drone legality, golden-hour logistics and upload bandwidth. Comfort is traded away for shot quality.

persona_catalog.label: Senior Citizen
persona_catalog.description: Traveller aged 60+. Optimises for medical fallback, low physical load, comfortable transport, rest stops, toilets, heat management and step-free access. Novelty and nightlife are near-zero weight.

persona_catalog.label: Child Friendly (3-12)
persona_catalog.description: Applied at entity level when children aged 3-12 are present. Stricter than family_trip: enforces age minimums on activities, weights engagement, safety and short attention-span logistics.

persona_catalog.label: Infant Friendly (0-2)
persona_catalog.description: Applied when an infant under 3 travels. Dominated by hygiene, medical proximity, stroller access, nap logistics, heat exposure, transfer duration and cot/changing availability. Most adventure activities are hard-gated out.

persona_catalog.label: Female Solo Traveller
persona_catalog.description: Woman travelling alone. Optimises for night safety, harassment levels, transport reliability, solo-dining and hostel/solo-social infrastructure, plus scam pressure. Hard safety floor.

persona_catalog.label: Pregnancy Friendly
persona_catalog.description: Pregnant traveller (typically 2nd trimester travel window). Dominated by obstetric access, Zika/vector risk, heat stress, exertion limits, food/water hygiene, motion sickness and flight duration. Hard-gates high-risk activities outright.

persona_catalog.label: Wheelchair Friendly
persona_catalog.description: Traveller is a wheelchair user or has a mobility device. Hard-gates anything without step-free viability. Weighted on step-free routing, accessible transport and toilets, lift availability, and surface quality.

persona_catalog.label: Road Trip Friendly
persona_catalog.description: Traveller wants to self-drive or use a private vehicle across a route. Weighted on drivability, road quality, scenic value, fuel/rest cadence, parking and road safety. Applies mostly to country/city/route entities.

persona_catalog.label: Couple Trip
persona_catalog.description: Two adults in a relationship, no children, no specific milestone occasion (that's honeymoon, a separate persona). Optimises for shared quality time, privacy, food and photogenic moments over group activities or nightlife. The default for an unadorned 'me and my wife/husband/partner' trip once no other persona (family, senior, occasion-specific) is detected.

persona_catalog.label: Young Couple (Romantic Getaway)
persona_catalog.description: Two young adults (roughly 18-30) travelling as a romantic pair, no children. A specialisation of 'couple': same privacy and photogenic priorities, but the archetype most real users picture for a young Thailand couples' trip is beaches, islands, sunsets, resort/beach-club energy and some nightlife — NOT the slow, calm, heritage-town vibe the generic 'couple' persona optimises for. This persona encodes that product expectation: it weights beach/island quality and value-for-money heavily, relaxes the strong 'must be uncrowded' pull that pushed older/quieter couples toward the northern hill towns, and keeps a light (not party-level) nightlife lean. See notes on this persona in derivePersonas — it is chosen over 'couple' only when explicit young-adult ages are present.

persona_catalog.label: Honeymoon
persona_catalog.description: Newly married couple celebrating a milestone occasion. Distinct from the generic 'couple' persona by materially higher weight on privacy/exclusivity, wellness and 'once in a lifetime' iconic experiences, and near-zero weight on cost efficiency — this is the one trip type where value-for-money is deliberately not the point.

persona_catalog.label: Luxury Traveller
persona_catalog.description: Optimises purely for quality — premium hospitality, low crowds, high safety and healthcare standards, mature tourist infrastructure — with deliberately no weight on cost efficiency at all (not opposed to spending, just indifferent to price as a factor). A modifier persona meant to stack with others (e.g. couple + luxury, family_trip + luxury) as much as stand alone.

persona_catalog.label: Budget Traveller
persona_catalog.description: Cost-conscious traveller optimising for low daily spend and genuine value, not luxury. The mirror image of the luxury persona — weights cost efficiency and value heavily, gives no special weight to spa/wellness/exclusivity signals, and is comfortable with hostel/backpacker-tier infrastructure as long as it's safe.

persona_catalog.label: Adventure Traveller
persona_catalog.description: Seeks physically engaging, outdoor, adrenaline-forward experiences — trekking, diving, ziplining, self-drive scenic routes. Deliberately does NOT weight low physical exertion (high exertion is often the draw, not a deterrent) — instead weights the safety STANDARDS around adventure activities (regulated water sports, road safety) and content novelty/offbeat appeal.

persona_catalog.label: Wellness Traveller
persona_catalog.description: Optimises for relaxation, spa, yoga and mindfulness — low crowds, quiet, comfortable weather, clean food, minimal physical exertion. Distinct from 'luxury' by weighting comfort/calm over exclusivity/status, and distinct from 'couple' by not weighting romance-adjacent signals at all — this persona applies equally to a solo wellness retreat.

persona_catalog.label: Foodie Traveller
persona_catalog.description: Trip organised around culinary experiences — street food, cooking classes, food markets, fine dining. Weights food hygiene heavily (a foodie eating widely and often is more exposed than an average traveller) alongside variety and accessibility signals (vegetarian/Indian food access, English for ordering).

persona_catalog.label: Digital Nomad
persona_catalog.description: Remote worker travelling with a laptop, needs reliable connectivity and a livable base for weeks at a time, not a sightseeing sprint. Hard-gates on workable wifi — everything else about the trip is secondary if the connection can't support a work day.

country.name: United Arab Emirates
country.summary: India's shortest-haul and highest-frequency outbound market: sub-4-hour flights from every Indian metro, near-hourly connectivity, universal English and Hindi, the largest Indian expatriate community anywhere, and a spread that covers skyline landmarks, desert, mall-scale shopping, calm Gulf beaches and mountains inside four small, road-connected emirates. The trade-off against Thailand is cost and heat, not infrastructure.
country.seasonality_note: The year is governed by heat, not rain: Nov-Mar is near-perfect (25-30°C) and is peak season; Jun-Sep is genuinely punishing (45°C+, high Gulf humidity) and pushes the whole trip indoors — outdoor activities (desert, beaches, Corniche, Jebel Jais) lose most of their value, though malls, museums and indoor attractions are unaffected.

provenance.source: UAE e-visa / visa-on-arrival policy for Indian passport holders (VoA for holders of a valid US/UK/EU visa or green card; pre-arranged e-visa otherwise). Not scored from a live source — treat as a directional prior only.
WHO Global Status Report on Road Safety — UAE sits well below the regional average and far below Thailand
CDC/WHO country risk classification — the UAE is malaria-free with no endemic Zika transmission; arid climate suppresses vector load
Composite of aggregated traveller-review sentiment, Numbeo safety indices and Travelomore desk research. Calibrated on the SAME rubric as Thailand so cross-country comparison is meaningful.
Airline schedule scrape (DEL/BOM/BLR/MAA/CCU/HYD → DXB/AUH/SHJ) + Travelomore booked-basket averages. The India-UAE corridor is among the densest international air routes in the world.
Municipal desalinated supply is treated to a potable standard at source, but rooftop-tank storage means bottled/filtered is the near-universal practice — scored filtered_only rather than safe.

cities.name: Sharjah
cities.summary: The UAE's cultural capital and its most conservative emirate: restored heritage quarters, the region's strongest Islamic-art museum, and a souk culture that Dubai has largely replaced with malls. Alcohol is illegal emirate-wide and nightlife effectively does not exist — which makes it the cheapest, quietest and most culturally intact base in the country, and the wrong one for a party trip.

meta.notes: beer_500ml_price_inr is deliberately ABSENT rather than zero or high: alcohol sale is illegal in Sharjah, so no legal price exists to score. A missing attribute drops the alcohol_affordability signal for this city instead of asserting a fabricated one; alcohol_access_index_0_100: 0 is what carries the real constraint.

cities.name: Ras Al Khaimah
cities.summary: The outdoors emirate and the closest the UAE gets to nature travel: Jebel Jais (the country's highest peak) with a genuinely spectacular mountain road, quiet shallow Gulf beaches, and desert camps without the Dubai queue. Cooler, emptier and cheaper than Dubai, but thinner on hospitals and public transport.

meta.notes: max_altitude_m is the CITY baseline (coastal/low foothills), not Jebel Jais — the 1900m summit is a property of the Jebel Jais activity, which carries its own max_altitude_m. Putting the summit altitude here would altitude-gate the entire emirate for pregnancy/senior personas over a single optional day trip.
